text.p: - Three Italian mountain climbers and one Slovenian died on Krn mountain in the northwestern Alps of Slovenia. This year 37 people have died in the Slovenian mountains.
- Slovenian president Milan Kucan is expected to name his candidate for prime minister of the new government on Monday after ending his talks with parliamentary parties.
- The ministry of defence spent $47.2 million on military communication systems this year. The Slovenian army bought most of its communication equipment from Israeli producer Tadiran.
- Most of Slovenia's coastal hotels will be full for the New Year celebrations, tour operators said.
- November unemployment in Slovenia rose 0.9 percent from October and fell three percent compared to the same period in 1995, the Statistical Office reported.

- Centre-left Liberal Democrats would get 33.7 percent of the vote if elections were held on Sunday, an opinion poll published by the paper said. The conservative People's Party would score 20.8 percent while its "Spring" alliance partner Social Democrats would get 9.6 percent.
- The number of stillborn children in Slovenia in 1995 decreased to 5.59 from 6.47 per 1,000 born in 1994.
- In Ljubljana there are some 300 homeless people, but only 29 of them have a bed in a public shelter designed for the homeless, city authorities said.
